QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_115

question.text: An arbitrageur identifies that Nifty futures are overpriced and tries to execute a cash-and-carry arbitrage by buying the Nifty basket of stocks. Due to liquidity constraints, he can only buy 48 of the 50 Nifty stocks and is unable to replicate the full index. What risk does this create?

answer.text: Tracking error risk - the 48-stock portfolio may not perfectly replicate the Nifty index, creating basis risk between portfolio performance and the index futures settlement
No additional risk because 48 out of 50 stocks is close enough for practical purposes
The arbitrage will be cancelled by the exchange because the replication is incomplete
The arbitrageur will be penalised by SEBI for attempting arbitrage with an incomplete basket

explanation.text: The Logic: Cash-and-carry arbitrage assumes the cash basket exactly mirrors the index. With only 48 of the 50 constituents in the basket, the portfolio's return can diverge from the index return depending on the weight and price moves of the two missing stocks - this is tracking error / basis risk and converts a notionally risk-free arbitrage into a risky position. The Trap: Exchanges do not cancel such trades and SEBI does not penalise the arbitrageur - the issue is purely an implementation/replication risk borne by the trader. Note: Source: NISM-Series-VIII workbook (Dec 2025), pages 49-53 (cash-and-carry arbitrage and imperfect index hedges).
